graphics: a behavioural probe contract shows the state record cannot be pinned yet, and refuses honestly  The fixed-function state record has words that could be rasterizer, blend, depth-stencil, topology, strip-cut, sample count/mask, quality or attachment fields, but nothing that says which. This adds a deterministic, GPU-free probe contract in port/src/graphics_pso: seven minimal scenes (opposite windings, two depth layers, overlapping blend layers, a triangle list, an indexed strip with a cut sentinel, a partial-sample cover, an out-of-range depth layer) rendered through a 4x4 RGBA8 target with per-sample depth, standard sample positions, blend, cull, depth clip, strip-cut assembly and a resolve, plus a contract table saying which scene decides which field group.  Measured against the title's 5,680 distinct state records: every field group leaves several candidate places, no place stores the fill-mode enum as a unit, the sample-mask domain is fully open, and attachments have no candidate place in the decoded container. The title's draws also supply no observation (no fragments - docs/frame_capture.md). So 0 of 8 fields are pinned, decode_fixed_function_state keeps refusing by name, and no guessed state is emitted. graphics_pso_test is 215 checks and graphics_record_test 158 (including a probe-input contract that every record word is copied verbatim); boot measured ALIVE with 10,000/10,000 records decoded and 10,000 pipelines created. docs/state_blob.md section 9 records the probe table, the decoded-vs-probed table and what a pin would need.

xg: decode the resource-layout record, make the linear layout the default, keep tiling refused  Console texture-layout slot 2 is GetResourceLayout with a 0x1B40-byte record, not the 0x6C8 previously assumed: a 0x18-byte header followed by four 0x6C8-byte planes (each 0x38 + 15 mips of 0x70). The offsets the title itself reads were pinned from both call sites, and the two records the title asks for (2048x2048 and 1024x1024 single-level R8) are filled exactly, with every non-field byte zeroed so no stack bytes survive. Slot 10 is GetResourceTiling (the seven-argument shape, 12-byte subresource entries); it stays refused with the field named, because a tile list only exists for a 64 KiB tiled resource and the window creates none - filling tile indices would be fabricated.  The linear layout is now the default path: the suggestion and texture-computer creation answer only for descriptions whose record can be written honestly (single level, single slice, 1D/2D, single sample, no render-target/depth flags, whole-byte single-plane format), and refuse by name for everything else (buffers, 3D, multiple mips/slices, MSAA, render-target/depth-stencil, planar formats). The measured A/B: 15/8 suggests/creations and zero copies in the old refusal path versus 44/24 suggestions/creations, two filled records and 65 copies / 34,044 B in the default path; both boots ALIVE with no exception, device loss or TDR, and the frame stays black (the content frontier is separate).  port/test/xg_xs_test.cpp grew to 86 checks (and 16 in the refusal arm); both gates green.

The constructor now inserts the heap the same way, with a comment naming the create_placed branch it feeds. Found by the full-build repair's d3d12_existing_heap_test, which the device-proxy contract documents as reaching the address branch.

streamed consumer: the 256 MiB of decompressed blocks are read by a title CPU deserializer and never named to the device  The 4,096 zlib file requests decompress 256 MiB in 2.3 s into 4,096 distinct process-heap destinations. A first-touch PAGE_GUARD diagnostic (read-only, off by default) shows the first eight blocks are read at ~2.3 s at the block head, by title code inside the deserializer function game+0x248F680, reached as a virtual method through the job-dispatch wrapper game+0x4F65820; the first bytes classify as structured binary (with one 16-byte repeating pattern), and blocks sampled from later batches are untouched in the window.  The GPU side is measured empty in the black-frame configuration: every device slot's first argument words and the copy-family console list slots were correlated, and no call names any of the 4,096 ranges - no heap or placed resource at a block address, no copy-family list call, no COPY queue or list created. So the streamed bytes die in CPU deserialization and never reach a texture.  The A/B with the console texture-layout path answering (linear mode) is the one where the title does name a streamed block (interior offsets) to console-addressed view creation calls and to console slot 70: the intended GPU naming exists behind the console layout answer, but our PC-shaped forwarding drops the Xbox-ABI address words and slot 70 is still refused. The doc records the caveat that the wrappers pass few arguments, so whether those words are true arguments is the next falsifier.  docs/streamed_consumer.md records the chain, the absence of the GPU step, the A/B naming, and the next measurement.
